description: Enfrentamos a exclusão digital, a desinformação nas escolas e o descaso político que limita a juventude a interesses particulares, negando-lhes preparo para grandes feitos. Criaremos uma ferramenta educativa e interativa que democratiza o acesso real à tecnologia, empoderando alunos e professores para o futuro. Buscamos jovens, devs, designers e educadores comprometidos com essa transformação. Venha somar conosco!
summary: Space Commander: Project Without Walls is an immersive, low-cost educational ecosystem developed by Team Oretti for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project combats digital exclusion and the lack of practical science and engineering education in vulnerable public schools, transforming basic Android smartphones into aerospace laboratories via low-cost Cardboard/VR Box headsets and offline-first WebVR technology (working without an internet connection).   Built on rigorous open NASA data regarding the Moon and Mars and aligned with Brazilian Space Agency (AEB) guidelines, the game applies four design rules—Dependency Network (central energy management), Three-Option Dilemmas, Short Cycles (Lunar Day and Night), and Immediate Visual Feedback—to teach engineering, systems thinking, public speaking, and active citizenship.   To overcome teacher digital illiteracy, the platform features an intuitive AI-assisted drag-and-drop Sandbox Mode, enabling educators to create and publish immersive lessons without coding. It also offers career exploration with scientist avatars and scales across multiple subjects in public school networks.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work? Space Commander: Project Without Walls is an immersive educational ecosystem developed by Team Oretti that transforms space mission planning (starting on the Moon and advancing to Mars) into a hands-on learning experience. Through an interactive offline-first game (capable of operating without an internet connection), students take on the role of commanders of extraterrestrial outposts and manage critical resources in short turns (such as Lunar Day, with high solar generation and intense radiation, and Lunar Night at -170 °C). The gameplay is built on four core design rules:

  • Dependency Network (The Domino Effect): Energy is the central resource powering Oxygen/Life Support, Radiation Shielding, and the Food Greenhouse; if energy levels drop, all other systems are immediately affected.
  • Three-Option Rule (Engineering Dilemmas): During crises (such as solar storms), players choose between protecting Area A while temporarily sacrificing Area B, protecting Area B while putting Area A at risk, or attempting to save both at double the resource cost and depleting emergency reserves.
  • Short-Cycle Rule: Fast-paced rounds demonstrate the immediate impact of current decisions on the next turn.
  • Immediate Visual Feedback: The 3D environment changes in real time according to system metrics (for example, if energy falls below 10, the screen darkens and red warning lights flash in the greenhouse).

Alongside the game, the platform features Sandbox Mode, an intuitive AI-assisted drag-and-drop dashboard that enables teachers to create and publish interactive lessons without writing any code.

2. What benefits does it bring and what is the intended impact? The project directly combats digital exclusion, teacher digital illiteracy, and the lack of practical science and engineering education in vulnerable public schools and community centers. By democratizing access to aerospace technology, it empowers educators as co-creators of content and fosters systems thinking, public speaking, community leadership, and active citizenship among students (through the Active Citizenship Simulator for collective resource management). Additionally, it includes virtual visits to robotics laboratories and innovation centers featuring avatars of real scientists to inspire STEM careers, and it can scale as a low-cost public educational policy across other disciplines (History, Geography, Environmental Studies, and Biotechnology).

3. Tools, programming languages, hardware, and software used

  • Software and Architecture: WebVR technology running directly in web browsers, an interactive 3D simulation engine, an offline-first architecture (local storage for operation without internet), and an Artificial Intelligence (AI) engine for dynamic student guidance and lesson-building assistance in Sandbox Mode.
  • Hardware: Engineered to run efficiently on basic Android smartphones paired with low-cost cardboard Virtual Reality headsets (Cardboard / VR Box), creating a "pocket planetarium," while remaining compatible with standalone VR headsets and school computers.
  • Scientific Data: Game logic grounded in rigorous open NASA data (lunar and Martian environmental parameters, radiation, thermal cycles, and life-support constraints) and aligned with the educational guidelines of the Brazilian Space Agency (AEB).

4. How is the project creative? Instead of requiring expensive computers, inaccessible physical laboratories, or high-speed internet, the project converts ordinary smartphones and cardboard viewers into immersive space laboratories. Combining genuine engineering trade-offs (without relying on heavy processing power) with an AI-assisted visual drag-and-drop editor simultaneously solves two historical barriers: the lack of school infrastructure and the technical hurdle preventing teachers from creating digital content.

5. What factors did the team consider? Team Oretti accounted for four critical factors regarding the reality of public schools:

  1. Limited infrastructure and lack of connectivity: Ensuring offline-first functionality and compatibility with entry-level smartphones.
  2. Budget constraints: Eliminating specialized hardware costs by leveraging Cardboard / VR Box viewers and browser-based execution.
  3. Teacher training and autonomy: Designing a no-code Sandbox Mode so educators can easily adopt and sustain the tool.
  4. Pedagogical rigor and sustainability: Aligning the curriculum with real NASA data and AEB guidelines while enabling ongoing scientific updates across public school networks.
